patients.label: 84-year-old man found after a long fall at home who developed shock in the ambulance

identity_evidence.quote: We present a case of an 84-year-old male

attribution_limitations: Cause of the unexpected shock is unresolved: the authors propose crush syndrome, spinal cord concussion and orthostatic hypotension as possible contributors and do not establish any one. These are hedged discussion statements and are kept review_only.

The initial assessment judged cervical spine injury unlikely, but a step-like protrusion around C5 to C6 was later noted and dislocated C3, C6 and C7 vertebrae were reported at follow-up. Both statements are kept; the method used to establish the dislocation is not stated and MRI was still awaited.

The sodium chloride sentence names intravenous access, and the next sentence and the abstract speak of intravenous fluid(s), but no sentence states the route of the sodium chloride itself; route and indication are left null rather than inferred from the fluid identity.

The abstract describes bruising to the chest and abdomen while the full assessment describes bruising/pooling along the anterior torso from neck to waist; treated as two descriptions of the same finding area, recorded from the full assessment wording.
Dehydration is described as likely developing but no measurement is reported; kept review_only.

The 154/119 mmHg value in the Table 1 initial observations and in the abstract "dropped from 154/119 mmHg" are recorded as one measurement because the abstract describes the drop from the pre-shock reading and no other pre-shock blood pressure is reported.

limitations: No figures or supplements are listed in the source, so there are no pixels to review.
Hedged causes of the shock and the dehydration statement are review_only; they are not asserted diagnoses.
The assessment environment (confined space, low-level lighting) and general guideline and literature statements in the discussion are not recorded as patient facts.
The method used to establish the C3, C6 and C7 dislocation is not stated.
